title: Side-hustle income and savings
oneLiner: Smooth irregular freelance income and keep the tax money separate.
goal: Establish what the customer's irregular income actually looks like, set aside what is not theirs to spend, and build a reserve that survives a quiet month.

stages.goal: Establish the real rhythm of the income from transactions - how often, how variable, how reliable. Ask how to get at it with `quick_replies`: `Use my transactions`, `I will describe it`.
stages.exitWhen: The pattern is described from actual data.

stages.goal: Separate what is not theirs to spend: tax, costs, refundable advances. Ask them to agree the proportion with `quick_replies` carrying their words and never a figure you chose: `That proportion works`, `Make it smaller`, `Not sure yet`.
Establish the monthly floor they must cover even in a bad month. If they do not know it, offer `quick_replies`: `Work it out from my transactions`, `I will give you a figure`.
Propose a structure that holds the set-aside separately and stays reachable. Ask whether it fits with `quick_replies`: `That works`, `Keep more reachable`, `Not now`.
Match to catalogue products and prepare one proposal, or save the plan.
stages.exitWhen: A proposal or saved plan exists.

mustEstablish: The actual frequency and variability of income, from transactions.
The worst recent month - that is what the plan has to survive, not the average.
What proportion is owed onward as tax or costs.
Whether payments arrive late, because that is a different problem from irregular.
neverDo: Never infer income, creditworthiness or business standing from follower counts, likes or engagement. Audience size is not revenue.
Do not plan against average income. Plan against the bad month.
Do not lock money away that a freelancer needs reachable. Liquidity beats yield here.
Do not treat an invoice as received money, or a client's promise as a payment.
Do not give tax advice. You can say 'set aside a proportion'; you cannot say what proportion the law requires.

objectionPaths.respondBy: Then propose a percentage-of-what-arrives rule rather than a fixed monthly amount, and say why that is the safer shape.
Be honest that the highest return usually means locked away, which is the wrong shape for irregular income. State the tradeoff and let them choose.

completion.default: The next action is explicit: prepare the set-aside account or deposit proposal, or save the irregular-income rule and review date.
completion.nivedita: Unlikely. If it is a small pension-supplementing activity, the next action is a simple set-aside rule that protects her income security.
completion.rhea: Likely secondary income alongside salary. The next action is a separate set-aside structure so it does not disappear into the household plan.
completion.ravi: His core journey. The next action is the invoice-aware set-aside rule after resolving the extra revisions in the client chat. Never touch his follower counts as a signal of anything.

openers: My freelance income is different every month and I cannot budget
I need to keep the tax money separate from the money I can spend
How do I save when I do not know what I will earn?
